transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess I’m here because I’ve been worrying a lot—more than feels normal for me. It’s like my mind just keeps finding things to latch onto. Work is a big one, with clients and whether deals will go through, and the market being so unpredictable. But it’s not just work. I worry about my family, and money, and even smaller decisions that should probably be settled by now.

For example, I recently moved to a condo, and I keep second-guessing whether that was the right decision, even though there’s no real disaster happening or anything. I can sort of recognize that the amount of worry I’m having doesn’t really match what’s actually going on, but I still can’t seem to stop turning things over in my head.
Do you notice any physical symptoms, like restlessness, muscle tension, trouble sleeping, or difficulty relaxing, when you’re feeling worried?

Yes, I do notice it physically, especially in my neck and shoulders. It’s not like sudden pain exactly, but by the end of the day they feel really tight, like I’ve been holding myself stiff or bracing for something all day without realizing it.

And I catch myself clenching my jaw too. Usually it’s when I’m driving between listings or sitting at my desk going over paperwork or emails. I’ll suddenly realize my teeth are pressed together and my shoulders are practically up near my ears. Then I try to relax them, but a few minutes later I’m doing it again. It’s frustrating because I don’t always feel like I’m “panicking” or anything dramatic—it’s more like my body is staying tense in the background while my mind keeps running through everything.
Have you been feeling this way—having a lot of anxiety and worry— most days over the past several months?

Yes… most days, I’d say. It’s been going on for quite a while now—about a year and two months, if I’m counting it right.

It really seemed to start after I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo. I mean, the move itself made sense on paper, and I can still explain all the reasons I did it, but after that I just didn’t seem to settle back down. Since then, the worrying has been there more days than not. Some days it’s more in the background, and other days it takes up a lot of space in my head, but it hasn’t really let up for any long stretch.
Do you find it hard to control or stop the worrying, even when you know it might be excessive or unnecessary?

Yes, I do. That’s actually one of the things that bothers me the most, because I can see, at least part of the time, that the worry is out of proportion. I’ll tell myself, “Parin, this is not urgent. You don’t need to solve this right now.” And I’ll mean it—I really will try to set it aside.

But then one concern sort of hands off to another. I’ll start with one small thing, like whether I responded to someone the right way or whether I missed a detail, and then it turns into replaying the whole conversation or going back over little decisions I already made. Before I know it, half an hour has gone by and I’m still thinking about something I meant to let go of five minutes after it came up.

It’s not that I want to be doing it. It feels like I’m trying to put something down, and my mind just keeps picking it back up.
